say.en: The folds, villi and microvilli of the small intestine multiply its inner surface hundreds of times over a plain tube. That is where almost all digested food enters the body. In this lesson: Explain the mechanisms of absorption.
Describe the absorption of fats via lacteals.
Describe common digestive disorders.

body.en: *Absorption* moves digested products from the gut into blood or lymph by simple diffusion (some glucose, amino acids, Cl⁻), facilitated transport (fructose, some amino acids), active transport against a gradient (glucose, amino acids, Na⁺) and passive water movement (osmosis). Fatty acids and glycerol, being insoluble, are first made into micelles, enter the mucosal cells, are re-formed into fats coated with protein (chylomicrons) and pass into the lacteals (lymph), then into the blood. Absorbed substances reach the tissues and are used (assimilation). The large intestine absorbs water, minerals and some drugs; faeces are egested by a voluntary reflex.

say.en: Turn on the folds, the villi and the microvilli. Each one multiplies the surface area; together they give hundreds of times the area of a plain tube.
Fatty acids and glycerol join bile salts as tiny micelles.
In the mucosal cell they are rebuilt into fats and coated with protein: chylomicrons.
Chylomicrons enter the lacteal, a lymph vessel, and later the blood.
Absorbing fats.

body.en: Jaundice: the liver is affected and bile pigments turn the skin and eyes yellow. Vomiting: ejection of stomach contents through the mouth, controlled by a centre in the medulla. Diarrhoea: abnormally frequent, watery stools, reducing *absorption*; it is treated with oral rehydration. Constipation: faeces retained in the rectum because bowel movements are irregular. Indigestion: food not properly digested, from too little enzyme, anxiety, food poisoning, overeating or spicy food. Protein-energy malnutrition causes marasmus (infants lacking both protein and calories) and kwashiorkor (protein lacking).

problem.en: Why is oral rehydration solution (salt, sugar and water) given in diarrhoea, and why does it contain glucose?

steps.en: Diarrhoea causes loss of water and salts, leading to dehydration.
Glucose is absorbed actively together with Na⁺ (co-transport), and water follows by osmosis.
So glucose speeds up the uptake of salt and water.

answer.en: To replace water and salts; glucose helps Na⁺ and water absorption

body.en: Sugars and amino acids go into blood capillaries; fats (as chylomicrons) go into lacteals — both start with "L": Lipids → Lacteal → Lymph.
